chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
One should endure like free people, otherwise one should keep quite like the ignorant.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of enduring like free people and remaining silent like the ignorant in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) contrasts the dignified restraint of the 'free' (al-Ahrar)—those who possess self-mastery—with the heedless silence of the 'ignorant' (al-Aghmar), who remain quiet merely due to lack of insight or opportunity. This teaching underscores the Shia ethical ideal that true nobility lies in conscious, virtuous patience rather than passive muteness, urging believers to cultivate inner refinement so their speech reflects wisdom rather than mere absence of noise.
